thread:
elaine: Quick sync on the benchmark launch creative and inbound routing. Need hero headline, 2 supporting charts, and routing tags for demo signups. Who's in?

matt: I can own the chart specs + CSV. Thinking: 1) small-multiples showing p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens across common configs, 2) stacked bars of cost per request by request-length bucket and quantization. Hero should be a clear econ delta vs a common baseline.

sarah: For headlines I'm drafting short variants. Roughs: A) "Serve faster. Spend less." B) "Real workloads, real run-rate savings." C) "Optimize serving, not models." Which lands?

elaine: I like the attitude in B but want something that mentions latency explicitly. Maybe tweak to: "Lower latency, lower token spend — in production."

matt: For the hero visual let's do a compact delta card: two horizontal callouts side-by-side. Left: p95 latency reduction (% and ms) vs baseline. Right: $/1k token delta with per-request example. Use arrows and short annotations.

zoe: I can wire the hero copy tests into the landing page experiment. We should capture which CTA converts better: "See demo" vs "Run your workload". Suggest adding hidden utm_tag for route=A vs B.

sarah: Color palette idea: keep core brand blue for Redwood, use neon-orange for our improvement deltas, muted gray for baselines. Accessibility check needed for orange on white.

ravi: Webinar funnel: top of funnel post -> gated landing with benchmarks -> optional interactive notebook for devs -> demo signup. For routing, tag signups by "workload_type" (chat, completion, embeddings, rerank) so sales can route.

matt: Chart implementation notes (CSV columns): model, variant, workload_slice, median_ms, p95_ms, cost_per_1k, request_length_bin, quant_level, throughput. Scatter is useful but small-multiples are easier for slides.

sarah: I'll prepare headline A/B copy and a few 1-liners for social. Short form for Twitter/X and longer for LinkedIn. Examples: "Reduce p95 by up to 35% on common chat flows." and "Cut per-request token cost without sacrificing latency."

elaine: Also need one sentence for the press/brief: "Redwood Inference benchmarks show production routing and serving optimizations can materially reduce latency and token economics across common LLM workloads." Keep it tight.

design-bot: Figma frame: https://www.figma.com/file/wxyz5678/benchmark-templates - hero_delta_card_v2. Use component tokens.

zoe: I'll set up two landing variants and wire UTM. Can we get the CSV by EOD so the page has real numbers?

matt: Yes, I'll push a sanitized CSV to the shared drive by 5pm. Will include baseline tag and notes on methodology.

elaine: Action list: matt - CSV + chart specs (EOD), sarah - copy variants + social teasers (tomorrow AM), zoe - landing splits + routing tags (tomorrow), design-bot - mock frames ready (in figma). Review in midday standup. :rocket:
